propositions: Packaged prose guides cite criterion ids inline (15+ in the plan guide) but no gate couples those citations to the registry, allowing criterion rubrics to be rewritten silently without invalidating the prose paraphrases.

When a criterion's authoritative registry text changes, the guide's claim about it must be re-verified and re-pinned, but currently no mechanism forces this verification or surfaces the divergence as a visible gate failure.

A new pin manifest (`criterion-pins.json`) derived from guide citations must be generated and validated in CI to convert invisible semantic drift into visible, forced re-verification: unknown citations, stale pins, orphan pins, and missing manifests are each reported by the gate.
The gate must be integrated into the existing `validate-routing` composition in `registry.py` without adding a new CI step or exceeding the 800-LOC module-size cap.

Citation extraction depends on the registry's closed criterion-id vocabulary matched at word boundaries with no structural markup dependence, so ordinary prose rewording and restructuring do not break the gate.
Regeneration of the pin manifest must be idempotent and canonical, and the committed manifest must remain in sync with the registry.
